gen-dafont-redux-gf-hanuman: Hanuman is a text serif with a high-waisted lowercase and terminals on the s set wide apart. And Redux above it spreads its geometric letters out, so a long passage reads unhurried and traditional.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-kadwa: Contemporary Redux spaces its geometric letters wide and lets each curve swing in with a visible entrance, while Kadwa's open-ended curves and large x-height carry the text. Give Kadwa a little extra size.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noticia-text: Noticia Text reads literary and dignified, its lowercase filling most of the letter height. Redux does its best work with stencil-cut letters and wide spacing, whereas Noticia Text keeps its entrance strokes and tall bodies for the running text.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-piazzolla: Wide, geometric, and a bit showy up top. Redux's stencil-free curves carry the thickening of a reed pen, while Piazzolla's serif lowercase nearly matches its capitals and its e opens like a pried clasp, so heading and text feel authoritative yet distinct.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-pridi: Pridi stands tall, its almost capital-sized small letters leaving generous gaps between curve ends and the stem. Redux's thick and thin strokes feel related, so a long page of this text serif goes down smoothly.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-slabo-13px: Slabo 13px is a classic serif with large open counters in its tall a, e and s. And Redux's wide spacing and subtle thick and thin cadence give the pair its strongest quality: a modern headline over a bookish voice.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum reads dignified, a text serif whose c is open as a bent paperclip. Redux spreads wide across the heading with hairlines that are present but not razor thin, while Suwannaphum's high, squared-off x-height holds the lines below.
gen-dafont-redux-inter: Wide spacing and a big visible entrance into every curved letter define Redux. Inter then takes over where Redux stops, its sans-serif lines smooth and tube-like, with breathing counters that suit text while Redux handles the heading.
gen-dafont-redux-rubik: Wide, geometric, and a touch springy. Redux keeps a tempered contrast in its curves, while Rubik's big lowercase and open round letters keep a plain sans paragraph soft and clear.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-archivo: SF Wonder Comic packs dense, tall words with bowls left open on one side and stems only a shade heavier than their arms. Archivo takes the other job, its commanding x-height and outward-opening curves doing the steady reading work.
